newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sees 5 pct US jobless rate possible.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sees 5 pct US jobless rate possible.

text.p: President Clinton said Friday he believes it is possible to have a 5 percent unemployment rate or lower without triggering inflation.

"I now think we have persuaded most economists that we can actually have a 5 percent or lower unemployment rate in this country without having inflation, if we do it with discipline," Clinton told a women's economic leadership forum.
Earlier on Friday, the Labor Department reported the jobless rate fell by 0.1 percentage point to 5.2 percent in March.
Clinton said a balanced budget would help, and he planned to work toward one.

"I'm going to do everything I can to get a balanced budget agreement this year, so that it will send a signal to the markets that they can keep interest rates modest, we can keep the market strong and we can keep creating jobs and bringing more and more people into the workforce," he said.
He described the 5.2 percent jobless rate as "misleading," saying many states were enjoying unemployment rates of 4 percent or less.
